topics.topic: RAM upgrade scorecard and next experiment
topics.section: 4. Upgrade tradeoffs; 5. Next read-only check and bounded experiment
topics.note: A 128 GB-class upgrade is not treated as sufficient from capacity alone. The gate is exact artifact/runtime compatibility followed by a bounded resident-memory, data-movement, quality, and operations canary.

topics.topic: DGX Spark 128 GB unified-memory capacity and bandwidth
topics.note: Current NVIDIA hardware documentation confirms a 128 GB coherent pool at 273 GB/s, shared by CPU, GPU, OS, runtime, model, and caches.

topics.topic: Transparent approximately 200 GB Spark plus RTX pool
topics.note: No transparent additive pool is claimed. Spark and the workstation remain separate systems unless an explicit distributed runtime partitions the model.

topics.topic: vLLM tensor and pipeline parallelism on mixed nodes
topics.note: Current vLLM documents TP, PP, identical execution environments, Ray, and network requirements. Uneven PP layer partitions exist, but heterogeneous Spark plus RTX support is not established.

topics.topic: SGLang pipeline parallelism and uneven layer partitioning
topics.note: Current SGLang docs retain manual PP layer partition controls. NVIDIA's Spark playbook validates a single-Spark setup, not this heterogeneous two-host combination.

topics.topic: PAIR as a model or memory pooling layer
topics.note: Current PAIR documentation explicitly describes routing each independent request to one node and disclaims model, memory, and in-flight request splitting. Its documented engines are Ollama and LM Studio.

topics.topic: Third-party heterogeneous Spark and RTX feasibility report
topics.note: The report remains compatibility evidence for its own hardware and network only. It is not used as primary evidence for RTX PRO 5000 support, performance, or quality.
